explanation: Issued Jan. 27; EO 13780 revoked it effective Mar. 16.
DOS identifies the effective period as Dec. 8, 2017–Jan. 20, 2021.

event_name: DOS Public Charge FAM Guidance Update
explanation: DOS revised public-charge guidance in January 2018, broadening the factors consular officers considered in immigrant visa adjudications. The guidance was rescinded following a July 2020 court injunction
Took effect May 31, 2019 and applied to immigrant visa applicants.
notes: Ongoing as of the end of the study period.

event_name: DOS Public Charge Interim Final Rule
explanation: Published October 11, 2019; implemented by DOS on February 24, 2020; enjoined July 29, 2020.
notes: Published in October 2019, but DOS implementation was delayed until February 24, 2020 after approval of Form DS-5540. The rule was enjoined on July 29, 2020

explanation: Restrictions took effect Feb. 21, 2020 and ended when PP9645/9983 were revoked Jan. 20, 2021.
notes: Restrictions on Burma, Eritrea, Kyrgyzstan, and Nigeria applied broadly to immigrant visas except certain SIVs; restrictions on Sudan and Tanzania applied to Diversity Visas.

event_name: Worldwide Suspension of Routine Visa Services
explanation: DOS announced the worldwide suspension of routine visa services on March 18, 2020. On July 22, 2020, embassies and consulates were allowed to begin a phased resumption of visa services based on local conditions and available resources.
notes: Routine visa services were suspended worldwide, while emergency and mission-critical services continued where resources allowed.

explanation: Presidential Proclamation 10014 took effect on April 23, 2020 and suspended entry of certain immigrants, subject to exceptions. It was extended twice but was revoked on February 24, 2021, before its scheduled March 31 expiration.
Routine visa services began resuming in July 2020, but capacity remained limited. In November 2021, DOS lifted its pandemic-era visa prioritization framework.
notes: November 2021 is used as an analytical endpoint for this recovery period, not as the date when consular capacity fully returned to pre-pandemic levels. DOS noted that some posts still faced COVID-related occupancy restrictions and staffing challenges after the prioritization framework was lifted.

explanation: DOS used a tiered system to prioritize immigrant visa processing during limited pandemic operations. The framework was lifted in November 2021.
notes: DOS rescinded the prioritization scheme on November 19, 2021, restoring broader post discretion over visa appointment priorities.

event_name: COVID-19 Vaccination Requirement for IV Applicants
explanation: CDC required immigrant visa applicants to complete a COVID-19 vaccine series beginning October 1, 2021. The requirement was removed on March 11, 2025.
DOS restored the pre-2019 public-charge regulatory framework effective October 5, 2023, changing the standards used in visa adjudication
notes: Ongoing as of the end of the study period.

explanation: Presidential Proclamation 10949 took effect on June 9, 2025 and fully or partially suspended visa issuance for nationals of 19 countries. It remained in effect until modified by PP10998 effective January 1, 2026.
Beginning November 1, 2025, NVC generally schedules immigrant visa applicants in their country of residence or, if requested, country of nationality
notes: Ongoing as of the end of the study period.

explanation: Effective January 1, 2026, PP10998 fully or partially suspended visa issuance for nationals of 39 countries and certain Palestinian Authority travel-document holders
notes: Ongoing through the end of the study period. PP10998 continued and expanded the restrictions previously imposed under PP10949.

explanation: DOS paused immigrant visa issuance for nationals of 75 countries beginning January 21, 2026. The pause ended on August 21, 2026.
notes: Applicants could continue submitting applications and attending interviews; the pause applied to immigrant visa issuance.
